_comment: ONE risk-path trigger table, fed through BOTH policy-half readers — the
desk-tools deskkit classifier (RiskPathTriggersFor + matchTrigger) and the
statusgen lint's duplicate (riskpathtriggers.go) — with identical expected
verdicts. This file is the cross-tree binding for mistake-proofing/01, modelled
on statusgen/testdata/roster_coupling.json: the two modules deliberately share
no code, so a shared VECTOR file is what keeps their duplicated readers honest.
A drift in either copy of the base list, the glob-matching rule, or the per-repo
topology reading fails a TriggerCoupling test in both modules.
POLICY HALF ONLY. Every case is the POLICY question — does this path match the
trigger set for this repo — never the mechanism half. The unknown-repo cases are
the discriminator: the desk classifier's MECHANISM half answers TRUE for an
unknown repo (fail-closed), but the POLICY half both readers must use answers by
the trigger set alone, so an unknown repo gets the base list only. A reader that
reached for RiskPathTriggered (the mechanism-gated accessor) instead of the
policy half would flip 'unknown repo, ordinary path' from false to true and
redden here. That is the reviewer's Q1 pinned as a case.
REFUSAL cases are what actually bind the two halves: an acceptance case only
proves the two agree on a good path. The glob-rule refusals (a directory-prefix
near-miss, the exact-segment-count rule for a '*' pattern) are where a rewritten
matchTrigger silently diverges.
The repos are the illustrative topology repos, not this house's real surfaces:
the per-repo triggers are adopter configuration now, and a fixture keyed to one
organisation's layout would not prove the cross-tree binding.
envExtra binds the THIRD leg — the additive ASSAY_RISK_PATH_TRIGGERS_EXTRA
adopter variable. Each side installs it through its own config transport, then
asserts the envCases both BEFORE (unset → does not match) and AFTER (set →
matches), so the env value is proven to be the cause, not a pre-existing trigger.

cases.why: base list applies to every repo: a secrets/ directory prefix
base list: the k8s rbac wildcard, exact 3-segment match
REFUSAL: an ordinary path matches no trigger
REFUSAL (glob rule): a '*' pattern is an EXACT segment count — 4 segments never match a 3-segment k8s/*/rbac.yaml
REFUSAL (dir-prefix rule): a segment that merely starts with 'secrets' is not the 'secrets/' prefix
per-repo topology trigger for the k8s repo: base/
per-repo topology trigger for the k8s repo: deploy/
the base list still applies on a repo that also has its own triggers
REFUSAL: an ordinary source path on the k8s repo matches none of its triggers
per-repo topology trigger for the toolkit repo: the gate code directory prefix
per-repo topology trigger for the toolkit repo: the write-guard command
REFUSAL: a desk COMMAND that is not one of the gate triggers (deskwt is not deskpost/deskboard/desktoken/deskpushguard/writeguard)
REFUSAL: the lint's own tree is not a trigger
POLICY-HALF DISCRIMINATOR: an unknown repo gets the base list only, so a base path still triggers (the mechanism half is NOT consulted here)
POLICY-HALF DISCRIMINATOR: an unknown repo with an ordinary path is NOT classed — a reader that used the mechanism-gated accessor would fail-close this to true

envCases.why: the additive ASSAY_RISK_PATH_TRIGGERS_EXTRA value widens the set for every repo — matches only when the env value is set
REFUSAL: the env value is additive, not a wildcard — an unrelated path still does not match even with it set
